question:
Given the following 3x3 system representing the intersection of three planes:

$x + 2y + 3z = 1$
$2x + 5y + 8z = 3$
$3x + 8y + 14z = 4$

(a) Use the matrix method to determine if the system has a unique solution.
(b) If so, find the solution vector $\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}$.
explanation:
(a) The coefficient matrix:
$A = \begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&5&8\\3&8&14\end{bmatrix}$

Calculate $|A|$:
$=1\begin{vmatrix}5&8\\8&14\end{vmatrix} -2\begin{vmatrix}2&8\\3&14\end{vmatrix} +3\begin{vmatrix}2&5\\3&8\end{vmatrix}$
$=1(5\times14-8\times8) -2(2\times14-8\times3) +3(2\times8-5\times3)$
$=1(70-64) -2(28-24) +3(16-15)$
$=1(6)-2(4)+3(1)=6-8+3=1$

So $|A|=1\ne0$, there is a unique solution.

(b) Find $A^{-1}$ (use cofactor/adjoint):
Row 1:
$A_{11}=\begin{vmatrix}5&8\\8&14\end{vmatrix}=70-64=6$
$A_{12}=-\begin{vmatrix}2&8\\3&14\end{vmatrix}=-(28-24)=-4$
$A_{13}=\begin{vmatrix}2&5\\3&8\end{vmatrix}=16-15=1$

Row 2:
$A_{21}=-\begin{vmatrix}2&3\\8&14\end{vmatrix}=-(2\cdot14-8\cdot3)=-(28-24)=-4$
$A_{22}=\begin{vmatrix}1&3\\3&14\end{vmatrix}=1\cdot14-3\cdot3=14-9=5$
$A_{23}=-\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\3&8\end{vmatrix}=-(1\cdot8-2\cdot3)=-(8-6)=-2$

Row 3:
$A_{31}=\begin{vmatrix}2&3\\5&8\end{vmatrix}=2\cdot8-3\cdot5=16-15=1$
$A_{32}=-\begin{vmatrix}1&3\\2&8\end{vmatrix}=-(1\cdot8-3\cdot2)=-(8-6)=-2$
$A_{33}=\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{vmatrix}=1\cdot5-2\cdot2=5-4=1$

Cofactor matrix:
$\begin{bmatrix}6&-4&1\\-4&5&-2\\1&-2&1\end{bmatrix}$
adjoint (transpose):
$\begin{bmatrix}6&-4&1\\-4&5&-2\\1&-2&1\end{bmatrix}$

$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}6&-4&1\\-4&5&-2\\1&-2&1\end{bmatrix}$

Multiply by $B=\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\\4\end{bmatrix}$:
First row: $6\cdot1-4\cdot3+1\cdot4=6-12+4=-2$
Second: $-4\cdot1+5\cdot3-2\cdot4=-4+15-8=3$
Third: $1\cdot1-2\cdot3+1\cdot4=1-6+4=-1$

So $X=\begin{bmatrix}-2\\3\\-1\end{bmatrix}$
Therefore $x=-2, y=3, z=-1$.

options.A:
(a) $|A|=0$, so the system does not have a unique solution.
(b) Therefore, a unique solution vector cannot be found.
options.B:
(a) $|A|=1\ne0$, so the system has a unique solution.
(b) $X=\begin{bmatrix}-2\\3\\-1\end{bmatrix}$.
options.C:
(a) $|A|=1\ne0$, so the system has a unique solution.
(b) $X=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-3\\1\end{bmatrix}$.
options.D:
(a) $|A|=-1\ne0$, so the system has no solution.
(b) No solution vector exists.
